question: What is the school bus "danger zone"?
choice_a: The area inside the bus near the emergency exits
choice_b: Only the area directly behind the rear bumper of the bus
choice_c: The area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger of being hit, either by another vehicle or their own bus
choice_d: The area within one bus length in front of the bus only
explanation: The manual defines the danger zone as the area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger of being hit, either by another vehicle or their own bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: How far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: As much as 50 feet, with the first 20 feet being the most dangerous
choice_b: As much as 10 feet, with the first 2 feet being the most dangerous
choice_c: As much as 30 feet, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous
choice_d: As much as 15 feet, with the first 5 feet being the most dangerous
explanation: The danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: How far does the danger zone extend from the left and right sides of the bus, and from behind the rear bumper?
choice_a: 20 feet from the sides and 30 feet behind the rear bumper
choice_b: 15 feet from the sides and 5 feet behind the rear bumper
choice_c: 10 feet from the sides and 10 feet behind the rear bumper
choice_d: 5 feet from the sides and 20 feet behind the rear bumper
explanation: The danger zones extend 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus and 10 feet behind the rear bumper.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: Which area is always considered dangerous, according to the manual, because of passing cars?
choice_a: The area directly under the bus
choice_b: The area to the right of the bus only
choice_c: The area to the left of the bus
choice_d: The roof of the bus
explanation: The area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: Where are the outside left and right side flat mirrors mounted on a school bus?
choice_a: Inside the bus above the windshield
choice_b: On the rear bumper
choice_c: At the left and right front corners of the bus, at the side or front of the windshield
choice_d: On the roof of the bus
explanation: The outside flat mirrors are mounted at the left and right front corners of the bus at the side or front of the windshield, used to monitor traffic, check clearances, and students on the sides and to the rear of the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.3 - Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: How far behind a school bus can the blind spot below and behind the flat mirrors extend?
choice_a: There is no blind spot when using flat mirrors
choice_b: The blind spot extends 5 to 150 feet, and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus
choice_c: The blind spot extends exactly 1,000 feet regardless of bus size
choice_d: The blind spot extends only 5 feet directly behind the bumper
explanation: The blind spot behind the bus extends 5 to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.3 - Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: If the outside flat mirrors are properly adjusted, how far behind the bus should the driver be able to see?
choice_a: 500 feet or 10 bus lengths behind the bus
choice_b: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus
choice_c: 100 feet or 2 bus lengths behind the bus
choice_d: 50 feet or 1 bus length behind the bus
explanation: Properly adjusted flat mirrors should let the driver see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus, along the sides of the bus, and the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.3 - Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: Where are the outside left and right side convex mirrors located?
choice_a: Below the outside flat mirrors
choice_b: Inside the bus near the driver's seat
choice_c: On the rear emergency door
choice_d: Above the outside flat mirrors
explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors and are used to monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.4 - Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: What is a characteristic of the view provided by the outside convex mirrors?
choice_a: They only show the sky
choice_b: They present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus
choice_c: They are used exclusively to check tire pressure
choice_d: They provide an exact, true-to-life size and distance view
explanation: Convex mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus, so the driver must ensure they are properly adjusted.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.4 - Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: When properly positioned, what should the outside convex mirrors let the driver see, according to the manual?
choice_a: Only the roof of the bus
choice_b: Only the front bumper
choice_c: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus
choice_d: Only the rear emergency door
explanation: Convex mirrors should be positioned to see the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.4 - Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: Where are the outside left and right side crossover mirrors mounted?
choice_a: On the roof at the center of the bus
choice_b: On both left and right front corners of the bus
choice_c: Inside the bus above the rear emergency door
choice_d: On the rear bumper only
explanation: Crossover mirrors are mounted on both left and right front corners of the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.5 - Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: What is the purpose of the crossover mirrors?
choice_a: To see only the rear window
choice_b: To see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus not visible by direct vision, and to view the danger zone to the sides including the service door and front wheel area
choice_c: To check tire tread depth
choice_d: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision, and to view the danger zone to the left and right side of the bus, including the service door and front wheel area.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.5 - Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: When crossover mirrors are properly adjusted, what should overlap according to the manual?
choice_a: Direct vision and mirror view vision, from the front bumper at ground level to a point where direct vision is possible
choice_b: The flat mirror and the interior mirror
choice_c: The left and right convex mirrors
choice_d: The overhead mirror and the rear window
explanation: The entire area in front of the bus from the front bumper at ground level to a point where direct vision is possible should be seen, and direct vision and mirror view vision should overlap.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.5 - Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: Besides the front bumper area, what else should properly adjusted crossover mirrors let the driver see?
choice_a: The right and left front tires touching the ground, and the area from the front of the bus to the service door
choice_b: Only the rear tires
choice_c: Only the fuel tank
choice_d: Only the roof vents
explanation: Crossover mirrors should also let the driver see the right and left front tires touching the ground and the area from the front of the bus to the service door.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.5 - Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror mounted?
choice_a: Below the dashboard
choice_b: On the front bumper
choice_c: Directly above the windshield on the driver's side area of the bus
choice_d: On the rear emergency door
explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver's side area of the bus and is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.6 - Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: How far behind the bus could the blind spot area associated with the overhead inside mirror extend?
choice_a: It begins at the rear bumper and could extend up to 400 feet or more behind the bus
choice_b: It extends only 10 feet behind the bus
choice_c: There is no blind spot associated with this mirror
choice_d: It extends exactly 50 feet behind the bus
explanation: There is a large blind spot area that begins at the rear bumper and could extend up to 400 feet or more behind the bus; the driver must use the exterior side mirrors to monitor traffic in this area.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.6 - Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: Besides the rear-bumper blind spot, where else is there a blind spot related to the overhead inside mirror?
choice_a: On the roof of the bus
choice_b: At the fuel filler door
choice_c: Directly behind the driver's seat
choice_d: In front of the windshield
explanation: There is a blind spot area directly behind the driver's seat, as well as a large blind spot that begins at the rear bumper.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.6 - Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: How should the overhead inside rearview mirror be positioned?
choice_a: To see only the road ahead
choice_b: To see the top of the rear window in the top of the mirror, and all of the students, including the heads of the students right behind the driver
choice_c: To see only the front tires
choice_d: To see the engine compartment
explanation: The mirror should be positioned to see the top of the rear window in the top of the mirror, and all of the students, including the heads of the students right behind the driver.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.1.6 - Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: According to the manual, when are more students killed?
choice_a: While the bus is parked at the school overnight
choice_b: While riding inside the bus as passengers
choice_c: While waiting at home before the bus arrives
choice_d: While getting on or off a school bus, more than while riding as passengers inside the bus
explanation: More students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside of a school bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2 - Loading and Unloading

question: Who must approve a school bus stop location before it is used?
choice_a: The school district must approve all stops before they are used
choice_b: Only the driver may decide, with no approval needed
choice_c: The state department of motor vehicles for every individual stop
choice_d: The bus manufacturer
explanation: Each school district establishes official routes and official school bus stops, and all stops should be approved by the school district prior to making the stop.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: When approaching a school bus stop and if the bus is so equipped, when should the alternating flashing amber warning lights be activated?
choice_a: At least 500 feet or approximately 30 seconds before the stop
choice_b: Only after the bus has already stopped
choice_c: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law
choice_d: At least 50 feet or approximately 1 second before the stop
explanation: If so equipped, activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop or in accordance with state law.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: When approaching a stop, when should the right turn signal indicator be turned on?
choice_a: About 10 feet before pulling over
choice_b: About 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over
choice_c: Only after the bus has come to a complete stop
choice_d: About 1,000 feet or approximately 20 seconds before pulling over
explanation: Turn on the right turn signal indicator about 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: When stopping, how far away from students at the designated stop should the school bus's front bumper be, and why?
choice_a: At least 50 feet away, to allow other traffic to pass
choice_b: There is no specified distance
choice_c: At least 10 feet away, which forces students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements
choice_d: Exactly 2 feet away, so students can board quickly
explanation: Bring the school bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop; this forces the students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: What should the driver do with the transmission and parking brake at each stop?
choice_a: Place the transmission in Park, or in Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and set the parking brake at each stop
choice_b: Shift to reverse and hold the brake pedal
choice_c: Turn off the engine but leave the transmission in gear
choice_d: Leave the transmission in Drive with no parking brake
explanation: When stopping, place the transmission in Park, or if there is no Park shift point, in Neutral, and set the parking brake at each stop.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: What should the driver do before completely opening the door and signaling students to approach?
choice_a: Sound the horn three times
choice_b: Release the parking brake
choice_c: Turn off all mirrors
choice_d: Make a final check to see that all traffic has stopped
explanation: The driver should make a final check to see that all traffic has stopped before completely opening the door and signaling students to approach.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: When should the alternating red lights be activated during a stop?
choice_a: Only after all students have boarded
choice_b: When traffic is a safe distance from the school bus, and the stop arm should be extended
choice_c: Never; only amber lights are used at a stop
choice_d: As soon as the driver sees the bus stop sign, regardless of traffic
explanation: Activate alternating red lights when traffic is a safe distance from the school bus and ensure the stop arm is extended.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: How should students wait for a school bus, according to the loading procedures?
choice_a: Standing in the roadway to flag the bus down
choice_b: Sitting on the curb with their backs to the road
choice_c: In a designated location, facing the bus as it approaches, and boarding only when signaled by the driver
choice_d: Anywhere along the road, running toward the bus as soon as it is visible
explanation: Students should wait in a designated location for the school bus, facing the bus as it approaches, and should board only when signaled by the driver.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: What should a driver do if a student is missing while counting students at the bus stop?
choice_a: Assume the student is absent and continue the route
choice_b: Ask the other students where the missing student is
choice_c: Leave immediately and report it later
choice_d: Call the police before checking with other students
explanation: Count the number of students at the bus stop and be sure all board the bus; if a student is missing, ask the other students where the student is.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: How should students board the school bus, and what light should be on when loading in the dark?
choice_a: Quickly and in any order, with headlights turned off
choice_b: Two at a time through the emergency door
choice_c: In single file without using the handrail
choice_d: Slowly, in single file, using the handrail, with the dome light on while loading in the dark
explanation: Have the students board the school bus slowly, in single file, and use the handrail; the dome light should be on while loading in the dark.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: Before moving the bus after loading, what should the driver wait for?
choice_a: Wait until the bus behind has passed
choice_b: Wait exactly 60 seconds regardless of student seating
choice_c: There is no need to wait once the door is closed
choice_d: Wait until students are seated and facing forward before moving the bus
explanation: The driver should wait until students are seated and facing forward before moving the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: If a driver cannot account for a student outside the bus during loading, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
choice_b: Honk the horn and continue the route
choice_c: Drive away immediately and call the school later
choice_d: Ask a passing motorist to search instead
explanation: If you cannot account for a student outside, secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: Once all students are accounted for after loading, what is part of the procedure to prepare to leave?
choice_a: Closing the door, engaging the transmission, releasing the parking brake, turning off alternating flashing red lights, and turning on the left turn signal
choice_b: Opening all windows and turning off the dome light
choice_c: Setting the parking brake and shutting off the engine
choice_d: Turning on the alternating amber lights and honking the horn
explanation: When all students are accounted for, prepare to leave by closing the door, engaging the transmission, releasing the parking brake, turning off alternating flashing red lights, turning on the left turn signal, checking all mirrors again, and allowing congested traffic to disperse.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: When loading students at the school campus, what should the driver do besides positioning to supervise loading?
choice_a: Turn on the interior heater regardless of weather
choice_b: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_c: Open all emergency exits
choice_d: Leave the engine running and the key in the ignition
explanation: When students are loading at the school campus, the driver should turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: During unloading on the route, why should the driver count the number of students while unloading?
choice_a: To confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop
choice_b: To determine which students get a window seat next
choice_c: It is not necessary to count students while unloading
choice_d: To report attendance to the school office
explanation: Count the number of students while unloading to confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: How far should students be told to walk away from the side of the bus after exiting on the route?
choice_a: Exactly 2 feet from the side of the bus
choice_b: At least 50 feet away from the bus
choice_c: There is no specific distance requirement
choice_d: At least 10 feet away from the side of the bus, to a position where the driver can plainly see all students
explanation: Tell students to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: According to the note in the manual, what should a driver do if they have missed a student's unloading stop?
choice_a: Do not back up; be sure to follow local procedures
choice_b: Immediately back the bus up to the stop
choice_c: Call the student's parents before doing anything else
choice_d: Continue the route and skip the stop permanently
explanation: The note states that if you have missed a student's unloading stop, do not back up; be sure to follow local procedures.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When students must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, how far should they first walk to a position where the driver can see them?
choice_a: Approximately 2 feet away from the bus
choice_b: Approximately 10 feet away from the side of the school bus
choice_c: Approximately 50 feet away from the bus
choice_d: There is no specified distance
explanation: Students should walk approximately 10 feet away from the side of the school bus to a position where the driver can see them.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Additional Procedures for Students That Must Cross the Roadway

question: How far in front of the right corner of the bumper should a crossing student walk, while still remaining away from the front of the bus?
choice_a: At least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper
choice_b: Exactly 1 foot in front of the bumper
choice_c: There is no distance specified for this location
choice_d: At least 30 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper
explanation: Students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, but still remaining away from the front of the school bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Additional Procedures for Students That Must Cross the Roadway

question: What should the driver be able to see when stopped at the right edge of the roadway before students cross?
choice_a: The student's feet
choice_b: The entire opposing lane of traffic only
choice_c: Only the student's head
choice_d: Nothing; visibility is not required at this point
explanation: Stop at the right edge of the roadway; you should be able to see the student's feet.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Additional Procedures for Students That Must Cross the Roadway

question: When students reach the edge of the roadway, what should they check regarding the bus's warning lights?
choice_a: Check that the dome light is off
choice_b: Check the fuel gauge
choice_c: Check to see if the red flashing lights on the bus are still flashing
choice_d: Check to see if the headlights are on
explanation: When students reach the edge of the roadway, they should stop and look in all directions and check to see if the red flashing lights on the bus are still flashing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Additional Procedures for Students That Must Cross the Roadway

question: Upon the driver's signal, where should students cross far enough to be?
choice_a: Far enough in front of the school bus to be in the driver's view
choice_b: Anywhere, as long as they hurry
choice_c: Directly beside the front bumper only
choice_d: Behind the bus, out of the driver's view
explanation: Upon the driver's signal, students should cross far enough in front of the school bus to be in the driver's view.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Additional Procedures for Students That Must Cross the Roadway

question: What should students do at the left edge of the school bus while crossing?
choice_a: Turn around and go back to the bus
choice_b: Stop and look again for the driver's signal to continue to cross the roadway
choice_c: Run across without stopping
choice_d: Wait for another vehicle to pass in the opposite lane before doing anything
explanation: Students should stop at the left edge of the school bus, stop, and look again for the driver's signal to continue to cross the roadway.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.3 - Additional Procedures for Students That Must Cross the Roadway

question: According to the manual, how do state and local laws for unloading at schools compare to unloading along the route?
choice_a: They are always identical
choice_b: They are often different, particularly for activities in a school parking lot or other location off the traveled roadway
choice_c: There are no laws governing unloading at schools
choice_d: Unloading at school requires no driver supervision at all
explanation: State and local laws and regulations regarding unloading students at schools, particularly off the traveled roadway, are often different than unloading along the school bus route.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.4 - Unloading Procedures at School

question: When unloading at school, what should the driver do to secure the bus before students exit?
choice_a: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_b: Open all windows and doors
choice_c: Set only the parking brake, with the engine running
choice_d: Leave the bus running with the door open
explanation: When unloading at the school, secure the bus by turning off the ignition switch and removing the key if leaving the driver's compartment.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.4 - Unloading Procedures at School

question: Compared to route unloading, what additional step is listed when preparing to leave after unloading at school?
choice_a: Opening the emergency exit windows
choice_b: Fastening the safety belt and starting the engine, in addition to closing the door and engaging the transmission
choice_c: Removing the ignition key and leaving it in the door lock
choice_d: Turning on the dome light
explanation: When leaving after unloading at school, the procedure includes closing the door, fastening the safety belt, starting the engine, engaging the transmission, releasing the parking brake, and other route-departure steps.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.4 - Unloading Procedures at School

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What should students be told to do if they drop an object near the bus during loading or unloading?
choice_a: Immediately pick it up themselves, even if it means stepping back near the bus
choice_b: Leave the dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, then attempt to get the driver's attention to retrieve it
choice_c: Ask another student to retrieve it from under the bus
choice_d: Ignore it and never mention it to the driver
explanation: Students should be told to leave any dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, then attempt to get the driver's attention to retrieve the object.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.5 - Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What is a "handrail hang-up" danger described in the manual?
choice_a: A student holding up the line at the top of the steps
choice_b: Students being injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or parts of their body get caught in the handrail or door as they exit the bus
choice_c: A malfunction that prevents the handrail from folding
choice_d: A student refusing to use the handrail at all
explanation: Handrail hang-ups occur when students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or even parts of their body get caught in the handrail or door as they exited the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.5 - Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What should the driver do to help prevent handrail hang-up injuries?
choice_a: Only check for hang-ups after the bus has already moved
choice_b: Remove the handrail entirely
choice_c: Instruct students to exit two at a time as fast as possible
choice_d: Closely observe all students exiting the bus to confirm they are in a safe location prior to moving the bus
explanation: The driver should closely observe all students exiting the bus to confirm that they are in a safe location prior to moving the bus, to help prevent handrail hang-up injuries.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.5 - Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

question: During the post-trip inspection, what should the driver look for while walking through and around the bus?
choice_a: Only whether the radio is turned off
choice_b: Articles left on the bus, sleeping students, open windows and doors, and damage or vandalism
choice_c: Only the fuel level
choice_d: Only tire pressure
explanation: The driver should look for articles left on the bus, sleeping students, open windows and doors, mechanical/operational problems, and damage or vandalism.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.6 - Post-trip Inspection

question: During post-trip inspection, which items unique to school buses require special attention when checking for mechanical/operational problems?
choice_a: The passenger reading lights only
choice_b: Mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms
choice_c: The cup holders
choice_d: The radio antenna only
explanation: Special attention should be given to items unique to school buses, such as mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.6 - Post-trip Inspection

question: What should a driver do if problems or special situations are found during a post-trip inspection?
choice_a: Wait until the next scheduled maintenance day to report them
choice_b: Ignore minor issues entirely
choice_c: Report them immediately to a supervisor or school authorities
choice_d: Fix them personally before the next route regardless of qualification
explanation: Any problems or special situations should be reported immediately to your supervisor or school authorities.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.2.6 - Post-trip Inspection

question: What is the first and most important consideration when determining the need to evacuate a bus?
choice_a: To wait for police to arrive
choice_b: For the driver to recognize the hazard
choice_c: To radio the school office for permission
choice_d: To count all students first, regardless of the danger
explanation: The first and most important consideration is for the driver to recognize the hazard; if time permits, the driver should contact the dispatcher before deciding to evacuate.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: As a general rule, how is student safety and control best maintained during an emergency or impending crisis?
choice_a: By immediately evacuating in every situation
choice_b: By having students exit through windows only
choice_c: By keeping students on the bus, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury
choice_d: By calling parents before making any decision
explanation: As a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: Which of these is listed among the mandatory evacuation conditions?
choice_a: It begins to rain lightly
choice_b: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_c: The bus is running five minutes late on its route
choice_d: A student asks to be let off early
explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when it is on fire or there is a threat of fire, when it is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing, when its position may change and increase danger, when there is imminent danger of collision, or when there is a need to evacuate due to a hazardous materials spill.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: Which condition is included in the list a driver should consider before deciding to evacuate a bus?
choice_a: Whether the bus route will run late
choice_b: Whether the students' parents have been contacted
choice_c: Whether moving students would complicate injuries such as neck and back injuries and fractures
choice_d: Whether the bus radio has a full battery
explanation: A decision to evacuate should include consideration of whether moving students would complicate injuries such as neck and back injuries and fractures, among other conditions like fire, fuel smell, and traffic danger.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: Why might it sometimes be safer to remain on the bus rather than evacuate, according to the manual?
choice_a: Because students must never leave the bus for any reason
choice_b: If there is a hazardous spill, it may be safer to remain on the bus and not come in contact with the material
choice_c: Because the driver is not permitted to open the doors
choice_d: Because evacuation is always against school policy
explanation: If there is a hazardous spill involved, sometimes it may be safer to remain on the bus and not come in contact with the material.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: When possible, how many responsible, older student assistants should be assigned to each emergency exit as part of emergency planning?
choice_a: One
choice_b: None; assistants are never assigned
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Four
explanation: When possible, assign two responsible, older student assistants to each emergency exit and teach them how to assist the other students off the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: How far off the road, and in what direction, should a "safe place" be located during an evacuation?
choice_a: At least 100 feet off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic
choice_b: At least 500 feet off the road, away from oncoming traffic
choice_c: Exactly 50 feet off the road, behind the bus
choice_d: At least 10 feet off the road, in any direction
explanation: A safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials, how far upwind of the bus should students be led?
choice_a: At least 300 feet
choice_b: At least 30 feet
choice_c: At least 1,000 feet
choice_d: At least 50 feet
explanation: Lead students upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: If evacuation is ordered while the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado, what should the driver do if shelter in a building is not available?
choice_a: Escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert and direct them to lie face down with hands covering their heads
choice_b: Keep all students seated inside the bus regardless of the tornado
choice_c: Drive the bus directly away from the tornado at high speed
choice_d: Have students stand and watch the tornado from a safe distance
explanation: If the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado and evacuation is ordered, escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert if shelter in a building is not readily available, and direct them to lie face down with hands covering their head, far enough away that the bus cannot topple on them.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: As part of securing the bus before an evacuation, what should the driver do with the transmission and parking brakes?
choice_a: Place the transmission in Park, or Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and set the parking brakes
choice_b: Leave the parking brake off in case the bus needs to be pushed
choice_c: Shift into reverse gear
choice_d: Leave the transmission in Drive to allow quick movement later
explanation: As part of securing the bus, place the transmission in Park, or Neutral if there is no shift point, and set the parking brakes.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: If there is no working radio during an emergency, what is the last-resort option described for getting help?
choice_a: Wait quietly until someone happens to drive by
choice_b: Dispatch two older, responsible students to go for help
choice_c: Have the driver leave the students alone to seek help
choice_d: Send all students together to find help
explanation: If no radio, or the radio is inoperable, dispatch a passing motorist or area resident to call for help; as a last resort, dispatch two older, responsible students to go for help.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: What does the manual say about moving a student believed to have a neck or spinal injury during evacuation?
choice_a: Move the student only if they ask to be moved
choice_b: Move the student to the front of the bus immediately
choice_c: Do not move the student unless his or her life is in immediate danger
choice_d: Always move the student first, before anyone else
explanation: Do not move a student you believe may have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger; special procedures must be used to move such victims.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: What characterizes a "passive" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It requires a police officer to be present at all times
choice_b: It does not have any type of traffic control device, and the decision to proceed rests entirely with the driver
choice_c: It has flashing red lights and gates
choice_d: It is only found on interstate highways
explanation: A passive crossing does not have any type of traffic control device; you must stop and the decision to proceed rests entirely in your hands.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.1 - Types of Crossings

question: What devices help a driver recognize a passive railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: Yellow circular advance warning signs, pavement markings, and cross-bucks
choice_b: Flashing red lights with bells and gates
choice_c: A police officer directing traffic
choice_d: A stoplight with a countdown timer
explanation: Passive crossings have yellow circular advance warning signs, pavement markings, and cross-bucks to assist in recognizing a crossing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.1 - Types of Crossings

question: What defines an "active" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It is only used by freight trains
choice_b: It has no signs or signals of any kind
choice_c: It is marked only with a yellow circular sign
choice_d: It has a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, such as flashing red lights with or without bells, or with bells and gates
explanation: An active crossing has a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, including flashing red lights with or without bells, and flashing red lights with bells and gates.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.1 - Types of Crossings

question: What does the round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign placed ahead of a railroad crossing tell the driver to do?
choice_a: Speed up to clear the crossing before a train arrives
choice_b: Sound the horn continuously
choice_c: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming
choice_d: Turn around and find another route
explanation: The advance warning sign tells you to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: What do pavement markings at a railroad crossing consist of?
choice_a: A single dashed white line
choice_b: An "X" with the letters "RR" and a no-passing marking on two-lane roads
choice_c: A checkerboard pattern
choice_d: A solid double yellow line only
explanation: Pavement markings consist of an "X" with the letters "RR" and a no-passing marking on two-lane roads, meaning the same as the advance warning sign.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: Where must the front of the school bus remain if there is a white stop line painted on the pavement before the tracks?
choice_a: Past the stop line but before the cross-buck
choice_b: Behind the stop line while stopped at the crossing
choice_c: On top of the stop line
choice_d: There is no requirement regarding the stop line
explanation: There may be a white stop line painted on the pavement before the railroad tracks; the front of the school bus must remain behind this line while stopped at the crossing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: What must a driver do at a cross-buck sign if there is no white line painted on the pavement?
choice_a: Ignore the cross-buck sign since it is only advisory
choice_b: Proceed without stopping if no train is visible
choice_c: Stop only if a train whistle is heard
choice_d: Stop the bus before the cross-buck sign
explanation: The cross-buck sign requires you to yield the right-of-way to the train; if there is no white line painted on the pavement, you must stop the bus before the cross-buck sign.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: What indicates the number of tracks when the road crosses more than one set of tracks at a cross-buck?
choice_a: A flashing blue light
choice_b: A sign below the cross-buck indicates the number of tracks
choice_c: The color of the cross-buck changes
choice_d: There is no way to know the number of tracks
explanation: When the road crosses over more than one set of tracks, a sign below the cross-buck indicates the number of tracks.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: What should a driver do when the flashing red light signals at a crossing begin to flash?
choice_a: Stop, because a train is approaching and the driver must yield the right-of-way
choice_b: Speed up to cross before the train arrives
choice_c: Only slow down slightly and proceed
choice_d: Ignore the lights if no train is visible yet
explanation: When the flashing red lights begin to flash, stop! A train is approaching, and you are required to yield the right-of-way to the train.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: At a gated crossing, when should the driver stop, and what should the driver do if the gate stays down after the train has passed?
choice_a: Stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers; if the gate stays down after the train passes, do not drive around it, but call the dispatcher
choice_b: There is no need to stop if the gate has not lowered yet
choice_c: Wait exactly 5 minutes before proceeding regardless of gate position
choice_d: Stop only after the gate has fully lowered, and drive around the gate if it stays down
explanation: Stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers across the road lane; if the gate stays down after the train passes, do not drive around the gate, but instead call your dispatcher.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: Approximately how far before a railroad crossing should a driver activate hazard lights?
choice_a: Only after stopping at the crossing
choice_b: Approximately 2,000 feet before the crossing
choice_c: Approximately 200 feet before the crossing
choice_d: Approximately 20 feet before the crossing
explanation: Approaching the crossing, activate hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing to make sure your intentions are known.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: What should a driver do while approaching a railroad crossing regarding gears and brakes?
choice_a: Shift into neutral and coast
choice_b: Apply the parking brake while still moving
choice_c: Accelerate to clear the crossing quickly
choice_d: Slow down, including shifting to a lower gear in a manual transmission bus, and test the brakes
explanation: Approaching the crossing, slow down, including shifting to a lower gear in a manual transmission bus, and test your brakes.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: At a railroad crossing, how close and how far should the bus stop from the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 5 feet and no farther than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: No closer than 50 feet and no farther than 100 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Exactly at the nearest rail
explanation: At the crossing, stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where you have the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: At the crossing, what should the driver do with the transmission and brakes after stopping?
choice_a: Place the transmission in Park, or Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and press down on the service brake or set the parking brakes
choice_b: Turn off the engine entirely before checking for trains
choice_c: Shift into reverse
choice_d: Leave the transmission in Drive with foot off the brake
explanation: At the crossing, place the transmission in Park, or Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and press down on the service brake or set the parking brakes.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: What should the driver do with radios and passengers at the crossing before looking and listening for a train?
choice_a: Have students sing to pass the time
choice_b: Turn the radio volume up to hear better
choice_c: Open all the windows and turn on the radio
choice_d: Turn off all radios and noisy equipment, and silence the passengers
explanation: At the crossing, turn off all radios and noisy equipment, and silence the passengers, then open the service door and driver's window to look and listen for an approaching train.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: At a multiple-track crossing, where should the driver stop, and what should be done before proceeding across all tracks?
choice_a: There is no need to stop at all if traveling slowly
choice_b: Stop between each set of tracks individually
choice_c: Stop only after crossing the last set of tracks
choice_d: Stop only before the first set of tracks, then when sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all tracks until completely cleared
explanation: At a multiple-track crossing, stop only before the first set of tracks; when sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all of the tracks until you have completely cleared them.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: In what gear should a bus cross railroad tracks, and should the driver change gears while crossing?
choice_a: Cross in the highest available gear
choice_b: Coast across in neutral
choice_c: Cross the tracks in a low gear and do not change gears while crossing
choice_d: Shift gears repeatedly while crossing for better control
explanation: Cross the tracks in a low gear; do not change gears while crossing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: If a gate comes down after the bus has started across the tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Back up off the tracks
choice_b: Drive through it even if it means breaking the gate
choice_c: Stop immediately on the tracks
choice_d: Wait for the gate to rise again before proceeding
explanation: If the gate comes down after you have started across, drive through it even if it means you will break the gate.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: If a bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving away from the tracks and toward the direction of the train
choice_b: Stay on the bus and wait for help
choice_c: Try to push the bus off the tracks alone
choice_d: Move everyone parallel to the tracks in either direction
explanation: If your bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, get everyone out and off the tracks immediately; move everyone far from the bus at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.4 - Special Situations

question: If there is no police officer at a malfunctioning crossing signal, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Wait indefinitely without taking any action
choice_b: Proceed immediately since the signal is malfunctioning
choice_c: Direct traffic personally at the crossing
choice_d: Call the dispatcher to report the situation and ask for instructions on how to proceed
explanation: If there is no police officer, and you believe the signal is malfunctioning, call your dispatcher to report the situation and ask for instructions on how to proceed.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.4 - Special Situations

question: What rule of thumb does the manual give for containment or storage area on the far side of a crossing?
choice_a: As a general rule, add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area
choice_b: The containment area does not need to exceed the bus length
choice_c: Add 100 feet to the length of the bus
choice_d: Subtract 15 feet from the length of the bus
explanation: As a general rule, add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area, summarized as "if it won't fit, don't commit."
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.4 - Special Situations

question: Even if active railroad signals indicate the tracks are clear, what must the driver still do at a passive crossing?
choice_a: Rely solely on the signals
choice_b: Look and listen to be sure it is safe to proceed
choice_c: Proceed without further checking
choice_d: Wait exactly one minute before crossing
explanation: Be especially careful at passive crossings; even if there are active railroad signals that indicate the tracks are clear, you must look and listen to be sure it is safe to proceed.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.4.4 - Special Situations

question: According to the manual, when should a driver deal with a behavior problem on the bus if it occurs during loading or unloading?
choice_a: Radio the school office and wait for a reply before continuing the route
choice_b: Wait until the students unloading are safely off the bus and have moved away; pull the bus over if necessary
choice_c: Never address behavior problems during a route
choice_d: Address it immediately, even while students are loading or unloading
explanation: If there is a behavior problem on the bus, wait until the students unloading are safely off the bus and have moved away; if necessary, pull the bus over to handle the problem.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.5.1 - Don't Deal with On-bus Problems When Loading and Unloading

question: When handling a serious problem on the bus, where should the driver stop and secure the bus?
choice_a: On the shoulder of a highway at highway speed
choice_b: There is no need to stop the bus for a serious problem
choice_c: In the middle of the travel lane
choice_d: In a safe location off the road, perhaps a parking lot or a driveway, and take the ignition key if leaving the seat
explanation: To handle a serious problem, stop the bus and park in a safe location off the road, perhaps a parking lot or a driveway, and secure the bus by taking the ignition key if you leave your seat.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.5.2 - Handling Serious Problems

question: How should a driver speak to an offending student when handling a serious behavior problem?
choice_a: Only through a written note
choice_b: Not at all; the driver should remain silent
choice_c: Angrily, to make clear the seriousness of the situation
choice_d: Respectfully, in a courteous manner with a firm voice, without showing anger, but showing that the driver means business
explanation: The driver should stand up and speak respectfully to the offender, in a courteous manner with a firm voice, remind the offender of expected behavior, not show anger, but show that the driver means business.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.5.2 - Handling Serious Problems

question: Where is a driver never permitted to put a student off the bus, except in specific locations?
choice_a: A student may only be put off the bus at a police station
choice_b: A student may be put off the bus anywhere as long as another adult is present
choice_c: A student may be put off the bus at any location the driver chooses
choice_d: Never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop
explanation: Never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.5.2 - Handling Serious Problems

question: If an offense is serious enough that the driver cannot safely drive the bus, who should the driver call?
choice_a: The student's friends to calm them down
choice_b: The bus manufacturer's customer service line
choice_c: No one; the driver should handle it alone
choice_d: A school administrator or the police to come and remove the student
explanation: If the offense is serious enough that the driver cannot safely drive the bus, call for a school administrator or the police to come and remove the student.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.5.2 - Handling Serious Problems

question: The Department of Transportation requires antilock braking systems on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 2000
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: January 1, 1998
choice_d: March 1, 1999
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires that antilock braking systems be on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.1 - Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: ABS is required on hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after what date?
choice_a: January 1, 2000
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: March 1, 1997
choice_d: March 1, 1999
explanation: ABS is required on hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.1 - Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp on a school bus's instrument panel?
choice_a: Red
choice_b: Yellow
choice_c: Green
choice_d: Blue
explanation: Your school bus will have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel if it is equipped with ABS.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.1 - Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What happens when a vehicle without ABS is braked hard on slippery surfaces?
choice_a: The wheels may lock up, and the driver may lose steering control or skid or spin the vehicle
choice_b: Nothing different happens compared to a vehicle with ABS
choice_c: The vehicle automatically slows down safely with no risk
choice_d: The brakes disengage automatically
explanation: When you brake hard on slippery surfaces in a vehicle without ABS, your wheels may lock up; when your steering wheels lock up you lose steering control, and when your other wheels lock up you may skid or even spin the vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.2 - How ABS Helps You

question: What does ABS help a driver do, according to the manual?
choice_a: Always stop in a shorter distance than without ABS
choice_b: Avoid wheel lock up and maintain control, and steer around an obstacle while braking
choice_c: Drive faster safely in all conditions
choice_d: Eliminate the need for regular brake maintenance
explanation: ABS helps you avoid wheel lock up and maintain control; you may or may not be able to stop faster with ABS, but you should be able to steer around an obstacle while braking.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.2 - How ABS Helps You

question: When braking a bus equipped with ABS in an emergency, what should the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Do not use the parking brake ever
choice_b: Do not pump the brakes
choice_c: Do not use the brakes at all
choice_d: Do not brake harder than 10 percent force
explanation: Brake the same way regardless of whether you have ABS on the bus; however, in emergency braking, do not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.3 - Braking with ABS

question: As you slow down using ABS, what should the driver do if it is safe?
choice_a: Pump the brakes rapidly
choice_b: Apply maximum brake pressure continuously
choice_c: Turn off the ABS system manually
choice_d: Monitor the bus and back off the brakes to stay in control
explanation: As you slow down, monitor your bus and back off the brakes, if it is safe to do so, to stay in control.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.3 - Braking with ABS

question: On older ABS systems, until what speed could the malfunction lamp stay on?
choice_a: It never goes off until the vehicle is serviced
choice_b: Until the vehicle has been driven ten miles
choice_c: Until you are driving over fifty mph
choice_d: Until you are driving over five mph
explanation: On older systems, the lamp could stay on until you are driving over five mph.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.4 - Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check or comes on while driving, what does this indicate?
choice_a: The bus's headlights are malfunctioning
choice_b: Nothing; it is a normal operating condition
choice_c: The entire braking system has failed completely
choice_d: The driver may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels
explanation: If the lamp stays on after the bulb check, or goes on once you are under way, you may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.4 - Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: What kind of skids will ABS help prevent, and what kind will it not prevent?
choice_a: ABS prevents all types of skids under all circumstances
choice_b: ABS only prevents skids caused by spinning the drive wheels
choice_c: ABS should prevent brake-induced skids but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_d: ABS prevents skids only in a turn, never during braking
explanation: ABS won't prevent power or turning skids; ABS should prevent brake-induced skids but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.5 - Safety Reminders

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten stopping distance, according to the manual?
choice_a: Yes; ABS always shortens stopping distance significantly
choice_b: Yes; ABS doubles the stopping power of the brakes
choice_c: ABS has no effect on stopping distance or vehicle control
choice_d: No; ABS will help maintain vehicle control, but not always shorten stopping distance
explanation: ABS won't necessarily shorten stopping distance; ABS will help maintain vehicle control, but not always shorten stopping distance.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.5 - Safety Reminders

question: When should the roof-mounted, white strobe light on a school bus be used, if the bus is equipped with one?
choice_a: Only during loading and unloading of students
choice_b: Continuously, at all times the bus is in operation
choice_c: When the driver has limited visibility
choice_d: Only at railroad crossings
explanation: If your bus is equipped with a roof-mounted, white strobe light, it should be used when you have limited visibility, meaning you cannot easily see around you.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.1 - Strobe Lights

question: What does the manual compare the side of a school bus to, in describing the effect of strong winds?
choice_a: An airplane wing
choice_b: A kite string
choice_c: A sail on a sailboat
choice_d: A parachute
explanation: The side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat; strong winds can push the school bus sideways and can even move it off the road or tip it over.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.2 - Driving in High Winds

question: If caught in strong winds, what should a school bus driver do?
choice_a: Keep a strong grip on the steering wheel, anticipate gusts, and slow down or pull off the roadway and wait
choice_b: Open the windows to reduce wind resistance
choice_c: Speed up to get through the windy area faster
choice_d: Turn off the headlights to reduce distraction
explanation: If caught in strong winds, keep a strong grip on the steering wheel and try to anticipate gusts; slow down to lessen the effect of the wind, or pull off the roadway and wait, and contact your dispatcher.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.2 - Driving in High Winds

question: According to the manual, when should a driver back a school bus?
choice_a: Routinely, as part of the normal route
choice_b: Only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle
choice_c: Only when students are present outside the bus to help guide
choice_d: Whenever it saves time on the route
explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged; you should back your bus only when you have no other safe way to move the vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 - Backing

question: What is the purpose of a lookout when backing a school bus, and what should the lookout not do?
choice_a: The lookout's only job is to hold the door open
choice_b: The lookout should direct the driver's steering the entire time
choice_c: The lookout warns about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, but should not give directions on how to back the bus
choice_d: The lookout should stand directly behind the bus at all times
explanation: The purpose of the lookout is to warn you about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles; the lookout should not give directions on how to back the bus.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 - Backing

question: If no lookout is available when a driver must back the bus, what steps should the driver take first?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, turn off the motor and take the keys, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear
choice_b: Back up immediately without leaving the driver's seat
choice_c: Honk the horn continuously and back up at normal speed
choice_d: Radio the school office and wait for permission before doing anything
explanation: If no lookout is available, set the parking brake, turn off the motor and take the keys with you, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 - Backing

question: At a student pick-up point, when must a driver back up, what should be done first?
choice_a: Back up first, then pick up students
choice_b: Pick up students before backing and watch for late comers at all times
choice_c: Have students stand behind the bus while it backs up
choice_d: Leave without the students if backing is required
explanation: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, be sure to pick up students before backing and watch for late comers at all times, and be sure all students are in the bus before backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 - Backing

question: How much tail swing can a school bus have, and what should the driver do to account for it?
choice_a: Up to a three-foot tail swing, so the driver should check mirrors before and during any turning movements
choice_b: Up to a one-foot tail swing, which requires no special mirror checks
choice_c: No tail swing occurs on modern school buses
choice_d: Up to a ten-foot tail swing, requiring a spotter at all times
explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing; the driver needs to check mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor the tail swing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.4 - Tail Swing
